paper.title: Global Regularization of the Spatial Elliptic Restricted Three-body Problem: Quaternionic, Hamiltonian Formulation
paper.abstract: Any objects in space may encounter singularity due to the inverse-square law of the gravitational force, hindering the analysis and propagation of particle motion in space. Regularization in celestial mechanics removes such gravitational singularities in equations of motion by transforming the time and coordinates. This paper addresses a class of regularization methods known as global regularization for restricted three-body problems (R3BPs), which simultaneously removes the two singularities (e.g., Earth and Moon in cislunar space). It enables analysis, propagation, and prediction of particle motion throughout the domain of R3BPs, which is in stark contrast to regularizing each singularity individually. In particular, this paper develops a formulation for global regularization of the spatial elliptic R3BP (ER3BP) under external perturbations. The presented formulation leverages mathematical tools from quaternionic (hyper-complex) algebra and Hamiltonian mechanics. This approach enables us to (i) elegantly handle the four-dimensional coordinates arising from the dimension-lifting operation for spatial regularization, (ii) systematically derive the coordinate-momentum transformation while preserving the canonical structure and incorporating perturbing forces, and (iii) provide geometric insights for analyzing the regularity of the transformation, resulting Hamiltonian, and dynamical flow. Numerical examples demonstrate the validity of the mathematical results as well as significant numerical benefits of the regularization formulation in perturbed Earth-Moon ER3BP.

paper.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
paper.abstract: Let $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,d) $ denote the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard balls moving freely in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We give a planar construction with exponential lower bound with respect to $n$: $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,2)\geq 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}, \quad n\geq3 $.

paper.title: H\"older regularity for metric Anosov flows
paper.abstract: We define a class of flows on compact metric spaces that we call \emph{$C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows}, $0 < \alpha < 1$ or $\alpha = \mathrm{Lip}$. We give verifiable criteria for a metric Anosov flow to be $C^\alpha$. We show that $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows have H\"older continuous local product structure, and in particular H\"older continuous holonomies. We deduce that topological conjugacies between $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows are automatically H\"older continuous. We show that any $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flow admits a strong (i.e. H\"older continuous) Markov coding. This yields strong ergodic properties for equilibrium states for H\"older potentials for $C^\alpha$ metric Anosov flows. The regularity of the local product structure is proved in a non-compact setting which applies for the geodesic flow on the universal cover of a locally CAT(-1) space. This allows us to obtain H\"older regularity results for the holonomy maps for pinched negative curvature manifolds with respect to the Sasaki metric. This contrasts with the result of Ballmann, Brin and Burns that there are examples in this class for which the dynamical distributions are not H\"older.

paper.title: Survivor Set of Gauss Map with a Hole at $1$
paper.abstract: Let $T$ be the Gauss map. For each $\alpha\in [0,1]$, let $E(\alpha)$ be the survivor set consisting of all $x\in [0,1]$ whose orbit $\{T^k(x):k\ge 0\}$ never enters the interval $(\alpha,1]$. We prove that the set-valued function $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ is increasing and locally constant almost everywhere. Moreover, we explicitly characterize all intervals where the function $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ remains constant. We also describe the points at which the map $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ is not locally constant. Further, we obtain the Hausdorff dimension of $E(\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in [0,1]$. We prove that the function $\alpha\mapsto \dim_H(E(\alpha))$ forms a devil's staircase on $(0,1]$, but is not continuous at $0$. This discontinuity implies that the result of Raith [Acta Math. Univ. Comenian. 63 (1994), 39-53] fails for piecewise monotone interval maps with infinitely many branches. Finally, we give an application quantifying the set of points sharing identical $\alpha$-continued fraction expansion and regular continued fraction expansion.

paper.title: On the Julia sets of the non-autonomous iteration of exponential maps
paper.abstract: This paper studies non-autonomous iterations of $\lambda e^z$, where at each step the parameter $\lambda$ is chosen from a bounded interval. Urba\'nski and Zdunik introduced and developed a thermodynamic formalism for random dynamics of exponential maps, extending the autonomous result established independently by Rees and Lyubich to typical parameter sequences in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$ with $1/e<A<B<\infty$. In this paper, we show that the same conclusion indeed holds for all parameters in $[A, B]^{\mathbb{N}}$, Our proof is based on carefully crafted uniform versions of pullback arguments, inspired by the original methods of Rees and Lyubich. In a related direction, Urba\'nski and Zdunik established a non-autonomous analogue of Misiurewicz's theorem for the exponential map, later refined by Lech. We further extend their work by providing a refined condition for the Julia set to be the entire complex plane.

paper.title: Conley Index of Limit Cycles in Filippov Vector Fields
paper.abstract: Within the framework of multivalued dynamical systems, we compute the Conley index for a class of limit cycles in planar Filippov systems. We classify these cycles according to their interaction with the switching manifold, including crossing, sliding, and mixed regimes. Using the Conley index for multivalued admissible maps developed by Mrozek, we construct the appropriate index pairs and determine the corresponding indices for each class. These computations enlarge the class of Filippov invariant sets for which the Conley index is known and extend previous results on low-codimension singularities to periodic dynamics.

paper.title: Stable Manifolds and Uniqueness of Parabolic Rays in the Newtonian $N$-Body Problem
paper.abstract: We study uniqueness for parabolic motions in the Newtonian $N$-body problem with a prescribed minimal normalized central configuration at infinity. A McGehee compactification identifies their tails with the strong stable manifold of the corresponding outgoing zero-energy equilibrium. The configuration projection of this manifold is locally a smooth graph, yielding a smooth initial-velocity field and uniqueness among all parabolic motions confined to a sufficiently narrow truncated cone, without any minimizing assumption. For parabolic geodesic rays, a renormalized action excess and a quantitative no-exit argument remove the confinement hypothesis when the initial configuration lies sufficiently far inside a smaller cone. We then prove that the set of collision-free initial configurations admitting more than one such ray has Lebesgue measure zero. The global argument propagates the local stable manifold backward, discards critical values of the configuration projections by Sard's theorem, and separates distinct regular branches through an explicit differential formula for their renormalized excess. No nondegeneracy assumption on the prescribed minimal central configuration is required. The proofs combine invariant-manifold theory with direct action comparisons and do not use weak KAM theory, Busemann functions, or the differentiability theory of Hamilton--Jacobi solutions.

paper.title: Dynamical Properties of Perturbed Weighted Shifts
paper.abstract: In this paper, sufficient conditions are established for diagonal perturbations of weighted shifts to be supercyclic, hypercyclic, and frequently hypercyclic, extending several classical results for weighted shifts to this more general setting. In addition, a complete analytic characterization of the shadowing property for these operators is obtained. Consequently, examples of frequently hypercyclic perturbed weighted shifts with the shadowing property are constructed.

paper.title: Computation of Attractor Lattices for a Class of Hybrid Systems
paper.abstract: We study the attractor lattice of a class of hybrid dynamical systems on compact metric spaces. Under the trapping guard condition, we prove that hybrid attractors form a bounded distributive lattice isomorphic to the attractor lattice of an associated semiflow. The regularized preimages define a lattice epimorphism from a sublattice of the regular closed, attracting neighborhoods of the semiflow onto those of the hybrid system, and from the whole lattice when the guard set and its reset image have empty interior. Then, using grids on the state space, we construct a convergent cofiltration of outer approximations of a fixed-time map of this semiflow. This construction realizes every finite sublattice of hybrid attractors by a lattice of attracting neighborhoods that are unions of grid elements at sufficiently fine resolutions, and provides index pairs for computing Conley indices. We illustrate these constructions computationally by extracting the Conley--Morse graphs of the bouncing ball, the rimless wheel, the spiking neuron, and exhibiting the attractor lattice for an impacting oscillator.

A convergent cofiltration of grid approximations realizes every finite attractor sublattice at fine enough resolutions and provides Conley index pairs.

paper.title: Sparsity and uniformity in dynamical Manin--Mumford problems
paper.abstract: For endomorphisms of the complex projective plane of a given degree, we prove that the existence of a special curve of bounded degree, in the sense of the dynamical Manin--Mumford conjecture, is confined to a proper algebraic subvariety of the parameter space. This confirms a conjecture of DeMarco and Mavraki in dimension two. For general regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb A^k$, we obtain a uniform dynamical Manin--Mumford bound outside an exceptional hypersurface. These results arise from a common strategy, valid in every dimension and codimension, which reduces such questions to the geometry of exceptional loci in the space of pairs formed by subvarieties and maps. We control these loci by combining arithmetic equidistribution, blender constructions, dynamical directions, monodromy arguments, and degenerations at the boundary of parameter space.

paper.title: Dimension of affine iterated function systems on $\mathbb{R}^d$
paper.abstract: Let $\{f_i(x)=M_ix+a_i\}_{i\in I}$ be an affine iterated function system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with attractor $\Lambda$, and let $\mu$ be an associated self-affine measure. Assume that the $M_i$ generate a Zariski dense subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb{R})$. Under the strong open set condition, we show that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\Lambda$ equals the affinity dimension and that $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mu$ equals the Lyapunov dimension. The above results are consequences of the following projection theorem, which requires no separation condition. For every $1\leq n\leq d$ and for Furstenberg measure a.e. $(d-n)$-dimensional subspace $V$, \[ \dim_{\mathrm{H}} (P^V)_*\mu=\min\{n,\,\dim_{\mathrm{H}}\mu\}. \] This projection theorem in fact holds under hypotheses weaker than Zariski density: simplicity of the Lyapunov spectrum and a mild transversality condition (the Oseledets non-concentration property). The source of dimension increment in our proof is the positive dimension of the fiberwise conditional measures, exploited through Wu's one-dimensional entropy increase theorem. A key ingredient in reducing the higher-dimensional problem to this setting is a new structural result: a slab-filling property of the measure.

analysis.tldr: Under Zariski density and the strong open set condition, attractor and self-affine measure dimensions equal affinity and Lyapunov dimensions, respectively. A separation-free projection theorem supports these conclusions.
analysis.problem: Determine Hausdorff dimensions of affine iterated-function-system attractors, measures, and their projections.
analysis.main_result: For an affine system on \(\mathbb R^d\) whose linear parts generate a Zariski-dense subgroup of \(\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb R)\), the strong open set condition gives the two dimension equalities. For every \(1\le n\le d\), Furstenberg-almost every \((d-n)\)-subspace gives projected measure dimension \(\min\{n,\dim_H\mu\}\), without separation. The projection result also holds under simple Lyapunov spectrum and Oseledets non-concentration.
analysis.context: Self-affine fractal geometry, projections, and entropy-driven dimension growth.

paper.title: Continuum-many discontinuous actions of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on manifolds
paper.abstract: For any $n\geq 1$, we construct a continuum of non-conjugate actions by homeomorphisms of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Q})$ on the $n$-sphere $S^{n}$ that do not extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{R})$. We do this by adapting a blow-up construction of Bowden and Mann. We motivate studying these actions and note down some related observations.

analysis.context: Group actions on manifolds and extension obstructions.

paper.title: The entry-exit function and nilpotent corrections in multidimensional slow-fast systems
paper.abstract: We study multidimensional entry-exit phenomena in slow-fast systems whose fast linearization contains a nilpotent component. We show that the classical spectral balance still determines the exit point as $\varepsilon \to 0$, however the nilpotent component induces an algebraic amplification invisible to the spectrum, producing a $\varepsilon|\log\varepsilon|$-shift of the exit point for $0 <\varepsilon \ll 1$. We further extend the analysis to systems with several spectral branches and show that mode dominance follows a hierarchical, lexicographic selection principle: accumulated spectral growth determines the leading order, while the nilpotent component resolves degeneracies between spectrally equivalent modes.

analysis.relevance_note: The slow-fast entry-exit analysis is ODE-centered without a stated connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: **Winding number forces universal synchronisation**
paper.abstract: We prove that two completely different oscillators synchronise through arbitrarily weak reciprocal impulses. Any two planar oscillators with hyperbolic attracting limit cycles and equal natural periods lock stably one-to-one under translation impulses with generic directions and a suitable range of positive strength ratios, whatever their vector fields, limit cycles and transverse contraction rates. The mechanism is topological: the winding of the asymptotic phase gradient forces phase advances and delays, and the relative winding number of an effective impulse field gives lower bounds on attracting and unstable locked states. Equal periods are not essential: locking persists under small nonzero mismatches, with persistence and loss governed by a shifted phase balance. The analysis covers the full state-dependent impulsive dynamics, including transverse stability. Nearly simultaneous emissions may make the return discontinuous; under an explicit regularity condition the global return has a normally attracting Lipschitz invariant circle with topologically Morse--Smale dynamics.

analysis.main_result: Generic translation directions and a suitable range of positive strength ratios yield stable one-to-one locking for the stated cycles. Relative winding gives lower bounds on attracting and unstable locked states; shifted phase balance describes small mismatches. Under an explicit but unstated regularity condition, the possibly discontinuous global return has a normally attracting Lipschitz invariant circle with topologically Morse-Smale dynamics.
analysis.context: Impulsive synchronization and topological return dynamics, including transverse stability.

paper.title: A Smooth Autonomous Flow with Exponential Mixing on the Three-Torus
paper.abstract: We construct a smooth autonomous divergence-free vector field on $\mathbb{T}^3$ whose flow is exponentially mixing with respect to Lebesgue measure. This answers an open question about smooth autonomous exponential mixing in three dimensions. Starting from an exponentially mixing Anosov suspension flow, we perform surgery near four periodic orbits and show that the resulting manifold is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{T}^3$. The resulting vector field has exactly sixteen hyperbolic equilibria. We also prove a general transfer theorem that preserves exponential mixing under certain singular changes of coordinates.

paper.title: Multivariate stable mixing local limit theorem for intermittent diffeomorphisms and flows
paper.abstract: We prove mixing local limit theorems for dynamical systems in the superdiffusive regime where there is convergence to a multivariate stable law (including the nonstandard domain of the central limit theorem). We apply our results to d-dimensional observables for intermittent maps and solenoids, as well as intermittent semiflows and flows.

paper.title: Translational tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets
paper.abstract: The periodic tiling conjecture asserts that if a bounded set $\Omega\subset \mathbb R^d$ of finite measure tiles $\mathbb R^d$ by translations, then it admits at least one fully periodic tiling. This conjecture was proved to hold in $\mathbb R$ by Lagarias and Wang, and was recently disproved by Greenfeld and Tao in sufficiently high dimensions. Its discrete analogue in $\mathbb Z^2$ was proved by Bhattacharya, whereas the conjecture in $\mathbb R^2$ remains open. In this paper, we analyze the structure of tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets: bounded open sets in $\mathbb R^2$ whose boundary is a finite union of line segments parallel to the axes. We prove that every such tiling that is topologically minimal is weakly periodic. Moreover, we show that if an axis-parallel polygonal set $\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^2$ then it admits a quasi-periodic tiling (i.e., a finite union of translated lattices). The proofs combine geometric decompositions of tilings with rational approximation and discrete tiling theory. As a consequence, we obtain that the translational tiling problem for axis-parallel polygonal sets with real algebraic vertex coordinates is decidable.

analysis.tldr: Topologically minimal tilings by axis-parallel polygonal sets are weakly periodic, and every such tile admitting a tiling admits a quasi-periodic one.
analysis.problem: Study translational tilings by bounded open planar sets with finitely many axis-parallel boundary segments.
analysis.main_result: Every topologically minimal tiling in this class is weakly periodic. Whenever a tile in the class tiles the plane, it has a tiling that is a finite union of translated lattices. For real algebraic vertex coordinates, the tiling problem is decidable; full periodicity in the plane is not claimed.
analysis.context: Translation tilings and the planar periodic tiling conjecture.

paper.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
paper.abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space. We keep their classification of singular sequences and replace the construction of the exceptional set by a direct exclusion: we use finite boundary charts for seven of the eight diagrams that can carry an unbounded four-product, and an exhaustive order census for Diagram 5. We derive the necessary mass conditions where needed and show that no germ with an unbounded four-product lies on a curve of normalized central configurations through a positive configuration. Five diagrams are excluded for all complex germs, two on curves through real configurations, and one on curves through positive configurations. Parts of the argument are computer-assisted: exact algebra, interval arithmetic and exact linear programming.

paper.title: Effective shadowing of transition maps for a Hamiltonian saddle-center-center equilibrium
paper.abstract: We introduce a general methodology to construct globally unstable trajectories near the normally hyperbolic invariant manifold (NHIM) of a saddle-center-center Hamiltonian equilibrium. The proposed approach builds upon the classical geometric mechanism of searching for trajectories near heteroclinic connections between invariant tori of the NHIM. The main ingredient is the Birkhoff normal form near the NHIM, which allows us to control the dynamics of the hyperbolic and center components. We construct transition maps on the NHIM that encode the dynamics along heteroclinic connections. By combining the transition maps with the inner dynamics, given by the restriction of the Hamiltonian flow to the NHIM, we show that these connections can be efficiently (in terms of the travel time) shadowed by true trajectories of the full Hamiltonian system. Finally, the efficiency of this methodology is illustrated in the case of the NHIM associated to the libration point $L_1$ of the Spatial Restricted 3-Body Problem (SR3BP) for the Sun-Earth system.

paper.title: Fatou Components of Attracting Skew Products: From Polynomial Classification to Transcendental Complexity
paper.abstract: We study the Fatou components of holomorphic skew products $F \colon \mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}^2, F(z,w) = (f(z) + r(z,w), g(w))$ near an attracting invariant fiber, introducing a refined classification of components on the fiber: bulging, partial bulging, and nowhere bulging. For polynomial skew products, we give a complete characterization of when the basin at infinity is non-bulging, and show that in this case non-bulging implies nowhere bulging, ruling out partial bulging entirely. In the transcendental setting, the behavior is richer: we construct partially bulging wandering domains and Baker domains, show that any orbitally unbounded Fatou component can be made nowhere bulging by choosing an appropriate function $r$, and prove that for any nonconstant $r$ there exists an entire function $f$ with an escaping wandering domain that fails to be bulging. Bulging thus depends on the interplay between fiber dynamics and perturbation.

In the transcendental setting, partially bulging wandering and Baker domains exist; suitable perturbations make orbitally unbounded components nowhere bulging, and each nonconstant perturbation admits an entire fiber map with a non-bulging escaping wandering domain. paper.title: On the singular set of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
paper.abstract: We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_\theta$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.

analysis.context: Nonpositive curvature, geodesic flows, and anisotropic regularity.

paper.title: Analytic Liouville Integrable Geodesic Flow Has Zero Entropy
paper.abstract: This paper studies the topological entropy of real-analytic Liouville integrable Hamiltonian systems. We prove that the Hamiltonian flow on a compact connected regular energy hypersurface has zero topological entropy whenever a complete family of commuting real-analytic first integrals is generically independent in a connected neighborhood of that hypersurface. The proof uses finite normal expansions along minimal analytic carriers and an ergodic version of Ziglin's leading-term argument to obtain independent invariant normal polynomials, whose Poisson geometry makes all tangent Lyapunov exponents of the carriers vanish. In particular, we prove that a real-analytic Liouville integrable geodesic flow on a closed real-analytic Riemannian manifold has zero topological entropy, giving a positive answer to the conjecture proposed by Paternain in 1992.

analysis.relevance_note: Zero topological entropy under analytic integrability is central to entropy theory.
analysis.tldr: Analytic Liouville integrability gives zero entropy on compact connected regular energy hypersurfaces under the stated neighborhood-independence hypothesis.
analysis.problem: Determine entropy of real-analytic integrable Hamiltonian and geodesic flows.
analysis.main_result: A complete commuting family of real-analytic first integrals, generically independent in a connected neighborhood of a compact connected regular energy hypersurface, forces zero topological entropy there. In particular, real-analytic Liouville integrable geodesic flows on closed real-analytic Riemannian manifolds have zero topological entropy.
methods: Finite normal expansions on minimal analytic carriers
Ergodic version of Ziglin's leading-term argument
analysis.context: Analytic integrability and entropy; the argument makes tangent Lyapunov exponents of the carriers vanish.

paper.title: On disjointness of 3-IETs from mixing and lightly mixing systems
paper.abstract: In this note we show that all interval exchange transformations of three intervals (3-IETs) are spectrally disjoint from all mixing and disjoint from lightly mixing systems. Until now, it was known that almost every 3-IET is rigid, which implies this property. However, not all 3-IETs are rigid, hence our result is a strict improvement of current knowledge. We then use this result, among many others, to prove that although some 3-IETs are mildly mixing, they are always disjoint in the sense of Furstenberg from lightly mixing systems.

analysis.relevance_note: Disjointness of interval exchanges from mixing systems connects directly to ergodic theory.
analysis.tldr: All three-interval exchanges are spectrally disjoint from mixing systems and disjoint from lightly mixing systems, including nonrigid examples.
analysis.problem: Extend known almost-everywhere disjointness results to all three-interval exchange transformations.
analysis.main_result: The result applies to every three-interval exchange, beyond the almost-everywhere rigidity argument. Even mildly mixing examples are Furstenberg-disjoint from lightly mixing systems. The proof methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Interval exchange transformations, spectral disjointness, and mixing.

paper.title: Essential factors for surface homeomorphisms
paper.abstract: Let $f$ be a homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least one that is isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism, possibly relative to a finite invariant set. We construct an intrinsic monotone factor by collapsing the maximal continua whose iterates have uniformly bounded diameter in the universal cover. The quotient is homeomorphic to the original surface and the factor is isotopic to $f$ and has several strongly chaotic dynamical features. It is infinitely continuum-wise expansive, tight, and topologically mixing, and it has a dense family of rotational horseshoes, dense periodic points, and a single topological homoclinic class. The factor can be taken as an area-preserving homeomorphism. The quotient preserves stable translation length on the fine curve graph and the applicable homological rotation sets. When $f$ is $C^\infty$, a companion paper gives a unique measure of maximal entropy for the factor; it has full support and is Bernoulli.

analysis.relevance_note: Monotone factors, mixing, expansiveness, and horseshoes are central topological-dynamics themes.
analysis.tldr: The authors build an intrinsic monotone factor of surface homeomorphisms in pseudo-Anosov isotopy classes with strong chaotic topological features.
analysis.problem: Extract an essential factor by collapsing continua with bounded universal-cover iterate diameters.
analysis.main_result: For a closed orientable surface of genus at least one and a homeomorphism isotopic to a pseudo-Anosov map, possibly relative to a finite invariant set, the quotient is the original surface. The factor is isotopic to the map, infinitely continuum-wise expansive, tight, mixing, with dense rotational horseshoes and periodic points and one topological homoclinic class; it can be area-preserving. Applicable homological rotation sets and fine-curve-graph stable translation length are preserved. For smooth maps, a unique full-support Bernoulli maximal-entropy measure is attributed to a companion paper.
analysis.context: Surface factors, pseudo-Anosov isotopy, and chaotic topological dynamics.

paper.title: Stably ergodic endomorphisms with positive Lyapunov exponents
paper.abstract: We introduce a new criterion which guarantees that a conservative local diffeomorphism is both non-uniformly expanding (in particular has all its Lyapunov exponents positive) and stably ergodic. The criterion involves averaging expansion rates over preimages and allows us to construct explicit examples in a variety of homotopy classes, including those represented by linear endomorphisms with contracting directions.

analysis.relevance_note: Stable ergodicity and nonuniform expansion connect to smooth ergodic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: A preimage-averaging criterion yields nonuniform expansion and stable ergodicity for conservative local diffeomorphisms.
analysis.problem: Construct stably ergodic expanding endomorphisms in diverse homotopy classes.
analysis.main_result: The criterion guarantees positive Lyapunov exponents and stable ergodicity, and gives examples even in homotopy classes represented by linear endomorphisms with contracting directions. The quantitative criterion and further hypotheses: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Conservative endomorphisms and robust ergodicity.

paper.title: On Sums of "Small" Cantor Sets
paper.abstract: We provide several results showing that sums of ``small'' Cantor sets can turn into an interval or a finite union of intervals. Specifically, we show that 1) There exists a Cantor set $C\subset [0,1]$ of zero logarithmic capacity such that $C+C=[0,2]$. 2) For any $n\ge 2$ there exists a Cantor set $C\subset [0,1]$ of zero logarithmic capacity such that a Minkowski sum of $n$ copies of $C$ is an interval $[0,n]$, while a sum of any smaller number of copies of $C$ is still a Cantor set. 3) For any $n\ge 2$ there exists a collection of Cantor sets $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_n\subset [0,1]$ of zero lower box-counting dimension such that a Minkowski sum of any $n-1$ sets from this collection is a Cantor set of zero lower box-counting dimension, while the sum of all $n$ sets is an interval $[0,n]$. 4) There is an uncountable family of Cantor sets of zero lower box-counting dimension such that the sum of any two different sets from this family is a finite union of intervals. 5) For each of the properties above, there are examples of Cantor sets with the same property having zero Hausdorff $h$-measure for an arbitrary given gauge function $h$.

analysis.relevance_note: Small Cantor sets, dimensions, and gauge Hausdorff measures are central fractal-geometry topics.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct very small Cantor sets whose Minkowski sums become intervals or finite unions of intervals.
analysis.problem: Determine how zero capacity, zero lower box dimension, or zero gauge Hausdorff measure coexist with large sumsets.
analysis.main_result: A zero-logarithmic-capacity Cantor set can have its double sum equal the full doubled interval. For every integer \(n\ge2\), such a set can first become an interval at its \(n\)-fold sum. Collections of \(n\) zero-lower-box-dimensional Cantor sets can have every \((n-1)\)-set sum remain a zero-dimensional Cantor set while the full sum is an interval. An uncountable family can have every distinct pair sum be a finite union of intervals. Analogous examples exist with zero Hausdorff measure for any prescribed gauge.
analysis.context: Fractal sumsets and the difference between small individual sets and large additive combinations.

paper.title: H\"older regularity of the top Lyapunov exponent for random matrix products with low-dimensional equator
paper.abstract: We investigate the regularity of Lyapunov exponents for products of random invertible matrices of arbitrary dimension $d\ge 2$. We prove that the top Lyapunov exponent is pointwise H\"older continuous with respect to the Wasserstein-Hausdorff distance in the space of probability measures with compact support, in the case where this exponent is simple and the equator has dimension equal to or less than one.

analysis.relevance_note: Regularity of random-matrix Lyapunov exponents connects to ergodic and smooth dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The top Lyapunov exponent is pointwise Hölder continuous when it is simple and the equator has dimension at most one.
analysis.problem: Study parameter regularity for compactly supported laws of invertible random matrices.
analysis.main_result: In every dimension \(d\ge2\), simplicity and the equator-dimension restriction yield pointwise Hölder continuity in the Wasserstein-Hausdorff distance on compactly supported probability measures. The Hölder exponent: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Random matrix products and Lyapunov-exponent regularity.

paper.title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem
paper.abstract: We show that finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for smooth diffeomorphisms. For every integer $R\geq2$, we construct a $\mathcal{C}^{\infty}$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ of a compact smooth manifold $M$ and a $T$-invariant probability measure $\mu$ such that $(T,\mu)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ for $\mathcal{C}^1(M)$ observables, but not of order $2R+2$. For some centred observable $f_0\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}(M)$, no subsequence of the normalised sums $\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f_0\circ T^i$ converges in distribution to a Gaussian law. In particular, exponential decay of two-point correlations implies neither exponential mixing of all orders nor the central limit theorem. We realise $(T,\mu)$ in two ways. In the first, $T$ is a fixed linear Anosov diffeomorphism of $\mathbb T^2$ and $\mu$ is singular with respect to Lebesgue measure. In the second, $M$ can be any compact smooth surface without boundary and $\mu$ is a physical measure whose statistical basin contains a nonempty open set. The main theorems have been formalised in Lean 4.

analysis.relevance_note: Mixing counterexamples and invariant measures connect strongly to ergodic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Finite-order exponential mixing need not imply a central limit theorem, even for smooth diffeomorphisms.
analysis.problem: Separate mixing orders and Gaussian limit behavior for smooth invariant-measure systems.
analysis.main_result: For each integer \(R\ge2\), a smooth compact-manifold diffeomorphism with invariant probability measure mixes exponentially to order \(R\) for continuously differentiable observables but not to order \(2R+2\). Some centered smooth observable has no subsequence of square-root-normalized sums converging to a Gaussian law. Realizations use either a fixed linear Anosov map on the two-torus with singular measure or any compact boundaryless smooth surface with a physical measure having a basin containing an open set.
methods: Lean 4 formalization of the main theorems
analysis.context: Higher-order mixing and probabilistic limit laws; two-point exponential correlation decay alone is insufficient.

paper.title: Alpern Lemma Independent of a Partition for Aperiodic Systems
paper.abstract: We prove that for every $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$, an aperiodic, probability preserving system and $\mathcal{P}$ a finite measurable partition of $X$, there exists an Alpern Multitower whose base is independent of $\mathcal{P}$. This removes the ergodicity assumption in the original proof of the independent Alpern Lemma of \cite{MR3373823}. As a consequence, we remove ergodicity assumption from recent results on limit theorems in deterministic systems \cite{Kosloff_Volny_2022,kosloffVolnyStableCLT,MR4955410}.

analysis.relevance_note: Independent towers for aperiodic probability-preserving systems connect to ergodic theory and partitions.
analysis.tldr: The independent Alpern multitower lemma holds for all aperiodic probability-preserving systems without ergodicity.
analysis.problem: Construct a multitower base independent of a prescribed finite measurable partition.
analysis.main_result: For every aperiodic probability-preserving system and finite measurable partition, an Alpern multitower with independent base exists. This removes ergodicity assumptions from the cited deterministic limit-theorem results, whose exact statements: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Ergodic-theoretic towers and deterministic limit laws.

paper.title: An application of the parameterization method to evolution flows associated to nonautonomous systems
paper.abstract: Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold of bounded geometry. We consider a time-dependent vector field $X : \mathbb{R} \times M \to TM$ with $X_t:=X(t,\cdot) \in \mathfrak{X}^r(M)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$ that satisfies some further uniform continuity assumptions. We suppose that $X$ admits a globally defined integral curve $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to M$. To any isolated subset $\Omega$ of the Sacker-Sell spectrum of $t \mapsto \nabla X_t(\gamma(t))$, Sacker-Sell theory associates a subbundle $\mathscr{N}^\Omega$ of $T_\gamma M$ invariant under $\nabla X_t$. Under additional nonresonance conditions on $\Omega$, we prove, by an application of the parameterization method (Cabr\'e et al., 2003), the existence of an invariant topological submanifold $\mathscr{W}^\Omega \subset \mathbb{R} \times M$ with $C^r$ fibers $W_t^\Omega:= \mathscr{W}^\Omega \cap \{t\} \times M$ that is unique in a sufficiently smooth subclass of invariant manifolds uniformly tangent to $\mathscr{N}^\Omega$ (made precise later). We moreover show regularity of $\mathscr{W}^\Omega$ with respect to parameters, and characterize the attraction towards $\mathscr{W}^\Omega$ via a foliation in the case $\Omega$ is the slowest part of the spectrum.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant manifolds and spectral bundles connect to smooth nonautonomous dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The parameterization method constructs invariant manifolds with smooth fibers associated to isolated Sacker-Sell spectral subsets, subject to further uniformity and nonresonance hypotheses.
analysis.problem: Construct and characterize spectral invariant manifolds along a global integral curve.
analysis.main_result: On a finite-dimensional complete bounded-geometry Riemannian manifold, a time-dependent vector field with the stated spatial regularity and further uniform continuity assumptions admits the claimed manifold under additional nonresonance conditions. Uniqueness holds in a sufficiently smooth uniformly tangent subclass; parameter regularity and attraction foliations are obtained when the spectral subset is slowest. The further assumptions and uniqueness threshold: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Spectral invariant manifolds and attraction in nonautonomous flows.

paper.title: Computational framework NetBiF predicts and classifies steady-state bifurcations in biochemical systems via reaction network structure
paper.abstract: Dynamics of biochemical systems are dictated by the stoichiometry and kinetics of reaction networks. These systems may admit positive steady states that could undergo qualitative change in response to varying rate parameters. These changes are called steady-state bifurcations, and they correspond to biologically meaningful processes. Classical bifurcation analysis relies on exact kinetics and rate parameters, which are often unknown or difficult to measure for complex systems. To address this, structural bifurcation analysis (SBA) was introduced to predict bifurcations using only the system's associated reaction network. In this work, the computational package NetBiF (Network Bifurcation Finder) is introduced to implement SBA. NetBiF is applied across diverse biochemical systems, including fundamental metabolic pathways, signaling and gene regulatory networks, and a large-scale carbon cycle model, to predict steady-state bifurcations. Crucially, for biochemical systems governed by power law kinetics, the implementation of NetBiF also classifies the steady-state bifurcations as saddle-node, transcritical, or pitchfork via a structural analog of Sotomayor's theorem. To this end, explicit formulations for the bifurcation criteria were derived for these biochemical systems. Determining and classifying bifurcation behaviors provide insight into biochemical systems' abilities to adapt to changing and fluctuating conditions. Collectively, the study presents NetBiF as a scalable, structure-based, and consistent computational tool to implement SBA. Our findings enable researchers to systematically study dynamical behaviors of biochemical systems through their reaction network structures without requiring explicit kinetic information.

analysis.relevance_note: Biochemical network bifurcation prediction is applied modeling without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Topological entropy of saturated sets for Lorenz attractors
paper.abstract: We study the topological entropy of saturated sets for continuous flows, with emphasis on singular hyperbolic dynamics. For a $C^r$-generic ($r \geq 2$) vector field $X$ carrying a geometric Lorenz attractor $\Lambda$, we prove that for every nonempty compact connected set $\mathcal{K} \subseteq \mathcal{M}(\Phi,\Lambda)$ and every open set $U \subseteq M$ with $U \cap \Lambda \neq \emptyset$, $h_{\mathrm{top}}(\Phi,G_{\mathcal{K}}(\Phi) \cap \operatorname{Trans}(\Phi,\Lambda) \cap U)=\inf_{\mu \in \mathcal{K}} h_\mu(\phi_1)$, where $\Phi=(\phi_t)_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ is the flow induced by $X$ and $\operatorname{Trans}(\Phi,\Lambda)$ denotes the set of points whose positive orbits are dense in $\Lambda$. The same formula holds $C^1$-generically for singular hyperbolic attractors. In contrast with the uniformly hyperbolic case, we also prove that, for vector fields in a dense subset of $\mathcal{X}^r(M^3)$, geometric Lorenz attractors admit a positive-entropy invariant measure with no generic points. An analogous conclusion holds for vector fields in a dense subset of $\mathcal{X}^1(M)$ whose non-trivial singular hyperbolic attractors contain singularities and satisfy $\dim E^{cu}=2$. These examples show that the discrete-time saturated entropy theory does not extend directly to singular flows.

analysis.relevance_note: Saturated-set topological entropy and singular-flow invariant measures are central.
analysis.tldr: Generic Lorenz and singular hyperbolic attractors obey a saturated entropy formula, while dense classes exhibit positive-entropy measures without generic points.
analysis.problem: Extend saturated-set entropy theory to continuous singular hyperbolic flows.
analysis.main_result: For a generic \(C^r\) vector field with \(r\ge2\) and geometric Lorenz attractor, every nonempty compact connected family of invariant measures and every open set meeting the attractor satisfy the stated formula: the entropy of saturated points with dense positive orbit in that open set equals the infimum of time-one measure entropies over the family. The formula also holds generically in \(C^1\) for singular hyperbolic attractors. Dense classes of geometric Lorenz examples have a positive-entropy measure without generic points; analogous singular hyperbolic examples require singularities and a two-dimensional center-unstable bundle.
analysis.context: Saturated entropy theory for singular flows; the counterexamples prevent a direct discrete-time extension.

paper.title: Nonuniform dichotomies via time rescaling
paper.abstract: We establish characterizations of general nonuniform dichotomies for linear nonautonomous dynamical systems in terms of nonuniform exponential dichotomies of appropriately time-rescaled systems. In discrete time, for a class of slowly growing rates, such a characterization requires an additional condition involving a suitable notion of nonuniform ordinary dichotomy, which can be omitted for invertible systems. In continuous time, we obtain a more general characterization for a large class of growth rates, without imposing this additional condition. Our approach does not rely on adapted Lyapunov norms and applies to evolution families on arbitrary Banach spaces. As applications, we show how several results concerning general nonuniform dichotomies can be derived from their counterparts for exponential dichotomies.

analysis.relevance_note: Dichotomies encode nonautonomous hyperbolic behavior and connect to the broader smooth-dynamics profile.
analysis.tldr: General nonuniform dichotomies can be characterized by exponential dichotomies after appropriate time rescaling.
analysis.problem: Relate growth-rate dichotomies to exponential ones in linear nonautonomous systems.
analysis.main_result: For slowly growing discrete-time rates, an additional nonuniform ordinary-dichotomy condition is required, but is omitted for invertible systems. Continuous time admits a broader class of growth rates without that extra condition. The approach applies to evolution families on arbitrary Banach spaces and does not require adapted Lyapunov norms. The precise rate classes: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Linear nonautonomous systems and nonuniform dichotomies.

paper.title: Coding multiplicity in self-similar sets on the line
paper.abstract: We study coding multiplicity for self-similar sets on the real line. When the similarity dimension exceeds one, almost every point with respect to the natural self-similar measure has infinitely many codings. We focus on the case when the similarity dimension is at most one. Our analysis proceeds through the recurrence properties and the size of the critical set, defined as the union of the pairwise intersections of the first-level pieces. Our main structural result shows that when the critical set is finite, unboundedness of coding multiplicity is equivalent to periodic recurrence to the critical set. Moreover, every commensurable system with a finite critical set has uniformly bounded coding multiplicity. This conclusion is sharp in the incommensurable setting. We construct a one-parameter family of four-map systems such that for Lebesgue almost every parameter, the critical set is a singleton and the open set condition fails, while the attractor contains a point with infinitely many codings. More generally, for transversal families, the set of parameters admitting an infinite coding fibre is dense among those for which the strong separation condition fails. We also obtain a quantitative lower bound for the Hausdorff dimension of this parameter set. Such parameters can form a meagre set. We continue the study of the geometric size of branching, obtaining dimension formulae for typical coding fibres and almost-sure upper bounds on the dimension of the critical set in transversal families. In contrast, we construct an exponentially separated system with no dimension drop whose critical set has the same Hausdorff dimension as the attractor and whose coding map has a fibre of continuum cardinality. Although we work in the one-dimensional setting, several results and arguments extend to higher dimensions.

analysis.relevance_note: Self-similar coding multiplicity, recurrence, and Hausdorff dimension are central.
analysis.tldr: Finite critical sets link unbounded coding multiplicity to periodic recurrence; commensurability forces a uniform coding bound, while incommensurable systems admit sharp counterexamples.
analysis.problem: Study coding fibers and critical-set geometry for self-similar sets on the line, especially at similarity dimension at most one.
analysis.main_result: With finite critical set, unbounded coding multiplicity is equivalent to periodic recurrence to that set, and commensurable systems have uniformly bounded multiplicity. A four-map family has, for almost every parameter, singleton critical set, failure of the open set condition, and an infinitely coded point. Transversal families have a dense infinite-fiber parameter set where strong separation fails, with a dimension lower bound. Further results concern typical fiber dimensions and critical-set upper bounds; an exponentially separated no-dimension-drop example has critical-set dimension equal to attractor dimension and a continuum-sized fiber.
analysis.context: Overlap geometry and symbolic coding of fractals; several results extend beyond the line.

paper.title: Existence and Uniqueness Proof for the Transport Equation and the Orthogonal Dynamics Equation for Zwanzig's Projection on Gaussian Spaces: A Vanishing Viscosity Method
paper.abstract: We prove the existence of unique solutions ${u\in H^1(0,T;L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))}$ of the transport equation $u_t=F\cdot\nabla u+f$ and the orthogonal dynamics equation ${u_t= Q_\text{Z} (F\cdot\nabla) Q_\text{Z} u+f}$, where $F$ is a time-independent vector field, $f$ is a forcing term, $P_\text{Z}=1-Q_\text{Z}$ is a Zwanzig projection (conditional expectation) on $L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)$ defined by $P_\text{Z}h \propto \int h(\cdot ,y) \rho(\cdot,y)\rm{d}y$, and $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian measure with density $\rho$. To this end, we develop a vanishing viscosity method based on the maximal regularity theory for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator on $L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The following assumptions guarantee the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions: ${f\in H^1(0,T;L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))}$, ${g\in H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)}$, $F\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $\rm{ess\,sup}_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(x\cdot F-\rm{div}F\right) < \infty$, where $g$ denotes the initial value function.

analysis.relevance_note: Transport and projected PDE well-posedness is not centrally connected to the stated entropy, fractal, or topological interests.

paper.title: Multidimensional Szemer\'edi Theorem for Pairwise Independent Jointly Intersective Polynomials
paper.abstract: We develop a new approach to the Joint Intersectivity Conjecture of Bergelson, Leibman, and Lesigne for commuting transformations. The conjecture asserts that the necessary divisibility condition is the only obstruction to polynomial multiple recurrence and, consequently, to the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'edi theorem. We establish the conjecture for pairwise independent polynomials, obtaining the first general result for sequences of arbitrary length beyond the classical one-transformation setting. Our argument is inspired by the Furstenberg-Katznelson approach and its polynomial enhancement due to Bergelson-Leibman. Its main novelty, however, lies in the development of new techniques that allow us to bypass the use of the polynomial van der Waerden theorem, on which these methods traditionally rely, and for which no suitable analogue is currently available in our setting. In particular, we prove a Nil-Bohr returns theorem for compact extensions in systems with nilpotent structure, as well as a nil-plus-null decomposition for polynomial multicorrelation sequences that preserves joint intersectivity and positivity.

analysis.relevance_note: Polynomial recurrence for commuting transformations and nilpotent structure connects centrally to group-action dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove the joint intersectivity conjecture for pairwise independent polynomials in the commuting-transformation setting.
analysis.problem: Determine whether joint divisibility is the only obstruction to polynomial multiple recurrence and the multidimensional polynomial Szemerédi theorem.
analysis.main_result: For pairwise independent polynomials, the conjecture holds for sequences of arbitrary length. A Nil-Bohr returns theorem for compact extensions in nilpotent-structure systems and a nil-plus-null multicorrelation decomposition preserve joint intersectivity and positivity. The full recurrence formula and definition of independence: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Multiple recurrence and polynomial patterns for commuting transformations; the argument bypasses polynomial van der Waerden theory.

paper.title: Analytic centralisers of quadratic germs and the Brjuno dichotomy
paper.abstract: For $Q_\alpha(z)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}z+z^2$ with $\alpha$ irrational, we prove that the analytic centraliser of $Q_\alpha$ is trivial whenever $Q_\alpha$ is not analytically linearizable. Together with the quadratic Brjuno--Yoccoz theorem this gives a complete dichotomy, for the centraliser is infinite cyclic at the non-Brjuno parameters and conjugate to the group of nonzero complex dilations at the Brjuno parameters. The result extends the dense-parameter conclusion of Avila--Cheraghi--Eliad to every nonlinearizable member of the quadratic family. The proof starts from Inou's graph-globalization construction, where we retain the original neutral fixed point on a Riemann surface and verify the branch topology and finite-valence estimate, including multiplicities. Nonlinearizability, through the equality case of Schwarz's lemma, forces the surface to be the plane, and a direct quadratic growth estimate then makes the two entire projections polynomial, so that the established polynomial commutant classification yields the integral-iterate conclusion. We also determine the convergence set of the formal commutants and classify the analytic iterative roots of every nonzero iterate.

analysis.relevance_note: Centralizers and linearizability connect to local complex dynamics; the abstract's use of trivial centralizer needs qualification.
analysis.tldr: For irrational quadratic germs, the author asserts a centralizer dichotomy between integral iterates in the nonlinearizable case and a group conjugate to nonzero dilations in the linearizable case.
analysis.problem: Classify analytic centralizers, formal-commutant convergence, and iterative roots for irrational quadratic germs.
analysis.main_result: For \(Q_\alpha(z)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}z+z^2\) with irrational \(\alpha\), the abstract calls the nonlinearizable centralizer trivial but explicitly describes it as infinite cyclic at non-Brjuno parameters; this digest interprets that wording only as the stated integral-iterate conclusion. At Brjuno parameters the centralizer is conjugate to nonzero complex dilations. Formal-commutant convergence sets and analytic roots of nonzero iterates are also classified, without the criteria being stated.
analysis.context: Local holomorphic dynamics and the Brjuno linearization dichotomy; the source's centralizer terminology is explicitly qualified.

paper.title: Stabilizers and maximal subgroups of topological full groups
paper.abstract: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Without assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness, we prove spatial rigidity for stabilizers acting minimally on infinite closed nowhere dense sets. Their isomorphism types determine the ambient Kakutani equivalence class and, when Hausdorff, the effective reduction. We also realize every AF groupoid with compact unit space as the full restriction, with its relative topology, of any minimal effective ample groupoid with Cantor unit space to a closed nowhere dense subset. Combining rigidity and realization yields continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic stabilizers in every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup; these stabilizers are maximal when the ambient groupoid is almost finite or purely infinite. The realization also gives explicit AF subquotients of the ambient reduced groupoid $C^*$-algebra, including the CAR algebra, with compatibility on the canonical diagonal subalgebras.

analysis.relevance_note: Cantor groupoids, stabilizer actions, and spatial rigidity are central group-action and topological-dynamics themes.
analysis.tldr: The author characterizes maximal closed-set stabilizers and proves rigidity and realization results for Cantor groupoids.
analysis.problem: Understand stabilizers in subgroups of topological full groups containing the commutator subgroup.
analysis.main_result: For minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space that are almost finite or purely infinite, maximality for a nonempty closed nowhere dense set is equivalent to minimality of the stabilizer action, minimality of regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Rigidity for minimally acting stabilizers on infinite such sets does not require almost finiteness or pure infiniteness. AF-groupoid realization yields continuum many nonisomorphic stabilizers, maximal in the stated almost finite or purely infinite cases.
methods: Realization of AF groupoids as closed-set restrictions
analysis.context: Topological full groups, Kakutani equivalence, groupoid reductions, and AF subquotients.

paper.title: Temporal invariance of evolutionary entropy and comparative demographic analysis
paper.abstract: Does evolutionary entropy depend on the width of the age classes used to describe a population? We show that the apparent dependence on temporal resolution is a consequence of the loss of information about reproductive timing within discrete classes. When this information is retained, corresponding continuous and discrete representations yield the same cycle entropy, generation time, evolutionary entropy, and reproductive potential in a common unit of time. When within-class timing is unknown, a uniform local reconstruction yields a logarithmic correction. For constant post-maturity hazard and fertility, continuous exponential and discrete geometric descriptions correspond exactly at every time scale. Thus, for a fixed reference duration, evolutionary entropy is a property of the reproductive process, not of its temporal partition. These results provide a mathematical basis for comparing demographic models across different temporal scales by identifying the information required to separate differences in reproductive organisation from effects of the chosen age-class representation.

analysis.relevance_note: Temporal invariance of entropy is the central mathematical question, although its application is demographic.
analysis.tldr: Continuous and discrete reproductive descriptions have identical entropy invariants when within-class timing is retained and time units agree.
analysis.problem: Determine how temporal partitioning affects evolutionary entropy.
analysis.main_result: Retaining reproductive timing within classes makes cycle entropy, generation time, evolutionary entropy, and reproductive potential equal across corresponding descriptions in a common time unit. Unknown timing with uniform local reconstruction yields a logarithmic correction. Constant post-maturity hazard and fertility give exact exponential/geometric correspondence at every scale. The correction formula: Not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: Nonlinear Feedback Control in High Dimensions using the Polynomial-Polynomial Regulator
paper.abstract: We consider the problem of computing Taylor approximations to the optimal feedback law and value function for infinite-horizon finite-dimensional nonlinear optimal control problem---also known as Al'brekht's method. The scalability of existing Al'brekht-based approaches to computing approximate solutions to the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation associated with the optimal control problem has been severely limited by computational resources. The computational time issue has been partially mitigated by recent works leveraging tensor-structure to develop efficient numerical methods. However, RAM requirements still have remained a major hindrance to scaling beyond state dimensions of a few hundred or low thousands. We propose an acceleration to compute the expensive higher-order terms in a reduced space, mitigating the curse of dimensionality. A fast and scalable \textsc{Matlab} implementation is provided open-source for general purpose use, with the ability to accommodate arbitrary polynomial nonlinearities in the control-affine state equation, as well as polynomial state-dependence in the cost function, and the ability to handle systems in generalized form with a non-identity mass matrix, such as finite element models. Combined with the exploitation of sparsity and modern low-rank Riccati solvers, this permits computing approximations to polynomial feedback laws based on Al'brekht's method in hundreds of thousands of states.

paper.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
paper.abstract: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.

paper.title: (Super-)fast convergence rates for Chernoff approximations via centered differences and Richardson extrapolation
paper.abstract: We use centered differences to construct Chernoff families and derive even asymptotic expansions for their iterated products. Richardson extrapolation is then used to cancel polynomial part and thereby raise the convergence order. As illustrations, we apply the construction to uniformly parabolic, Schr\"odinger-type second-order operators and to a third-order dispersive operator, obtaining, at extrapolation depth $m$, the rates $ O(n^{-2m}) $ on the Sobolev scales $H^{2m+\delta}$, $H^{4m}$, and $H^{5m}$, respectively, with arbitrary $\delta>0$. In the analytic category, quantitative all-order estimates allow the extrapolation depth to grow with the base resolution and yield the super-fast rates $e^{-cn^2}$ for the two second-order models and $e^{-cn} $ for the third-order model. The constructions are explicit in terms of the coefficients of the underlying differential operators and do not use the target semigroup in their definition. This provides a constructive positive answer to the challenge of super-fast Chernoff approximation formulated by Remizov in Problem 30 of arXiv:2410.00416.

paper.title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
paper.abstract: Motivated by a question of Hochman, we investigate whether two deterministic time measures or time sets can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Using rescaled correlation integrals, we give a criterion for mutual singularity of the laws of the image measures, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For self-similar time sets satisfying the open set condition, we also recover the natural occupation measure from the compact image. Together, these results allow us to distinguish lattice and non-lattice self-similar sets and their natural measures within this class. For a naturally parametrised family with two contractions, with fixed dimension, each parameter can be distinguished from all but finitely many others. If the dimension is sufficiently small, every distinct parameter can be distinguished.

paper.title: $\mathcal{D}$-Pullback Measure Attractors of McKean-Vlasov Stochastic Lattice Wave Equations
paper.abstract: This paper deals with the pullback measure attractor for a non-autonomous distribution-dependent stochastic lattice wave equation with nonlinear noise on $\mathbb{Z}$. We establish well-posedness in the energy space $\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2}$ and show that the solution generates a continuous non-autonomous dynamical system on $\mathcal{P}_{4}(\ell^{2}\times\ell^{2})$, which possesses a unique pullback measure attractor $\mathcal{A}$. Furthermore, we prove the convergence of the attractor $\mathcal{A}^{\varepsilon}$ as $\varepsilon\to 0^{+}$ to the attractor of the corresponding distribution-independent limit system.

paper.title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along Reiter Sequences on Locally Compact Groups
paper.abstract: Let $G$ be a locally compact, second countable group admitting a Reiter sequence, and suppose that $G$ acts on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ equipped with a semifinite trace $\tau$ via trace-preserving automorphisms. In this paper, we prove a maximal inequality for ergodic averages along such Reiter sequences. Our approach relies on approximating the Reiter sequence by a linear combination of characteristic functions of F{\o}lner sequences using the layer-cake representation. Furthermore, we establish the bilateral almost uniform convergence of these ergodic averages. As an application, we deduce a non-commutative Wiener-Wintner type theorem along Reiter sequences.

paper.title: $2$-large sets are sets of nil-Bohr recurrence
paper.abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $2$-large if every two-coloring contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every such set meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood \(B\) of \(0\) and every \(\eps>0\), restricting the common difference to \(B\) increases the extremal number for \(k\)-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of \(1+\eps\), provided \(k\) is sufficiently large.

paper.title: How Mobile Oscillators Reshape Dynamical Robustness in Complex Networks
paper.abstract: While the robustness of collective dynamics in static networks is well established, how agent mobility and network topology jointly shape dynamical robustness remains largely unexplored. In this letter, we investigate the robustness of mobile Stuart-Landau oscillators performing random walks on networks and interacting diffusively when co-located. In the rapid-mobility regime, we reduce the dynamics to a mean-field framework linking network degree statistics to an effective global coupling strength. We show analytically that increased degree heterogeneity in the network enhances the effective coupling strength, and strictly lowers the critical threshold of functional degradation for amplitude death. Numerical simulations confirm the predicted heterogeneity-dependent ordering of the transition thresholds, showing an earlier collective collapse in scale-free networks than in random or regular networks. Our results establish mobility and network heterogeneity as key determinants of robustness in mobile oscillator populations, with implications for resilient biological and engineered collectives.

paper.title: Spectral Measure and Tail Process for Multivariate Dynamical Extremes
paper.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of extreme events in multivariate stationary sequences, with particular emphasis on stochastic processes generated by dynamical systems. We develop a general framework for describing the dependence structure of extremes through two complementary objects: the tail process and the spectral measure. We first extend the enriched point-process convergence of the univariate theory to the multivariate setting, proving that the decorated point process of exceedances converges to a marked Poisson cluster process whose marks retain the componentwise and temporal structure of extreme clusters. We then construct a spectral measure for stationary sequences, which assigns weight to distinct extremal profiles and characterizes the asymptotic dependence between components, and establish a de Haan-Resnick type representation. We also relate the spectral measure to the tail process, showing that its normalized profile distribution is recovered from the angular component of the tail process. Finally, we recover the classical univariate and multivariate exceedance processes as special cases. We illustrate the theory through applications to dynamical systems, using examples in which different dynamical mechanisms give rise to distinct extremal clustering patterns and cross-dependence structures. These applications demonstrate the ability of the proposed framework to capture genuinely multivariate features of extreme events and to extract information about the underlying dynamics that is not accessible through classical exceedance processes.

paper.title: (Sharp arithmetic) localization beyond transversality
paper.abstract: We prove sharp arithmetic localization for one-dimensional quasiperiodic potentials with jump discontinuities, beyond uniform transversality. Our results include every non-constant $C^1$ monotone sampling function, even with arbitrarily large flat regions, and also certain non-monotone potentials. A key new mechanism is a symbolic unique-continuation principle: first-return words to the region where $f'>0$ have no common Dirichlet resonance, forcing eigenfunction mass to transfer away from flat or negatively sloped regions and recovering quantitative monotonicity of finite-volume eigenvalue branches.

paper.title: Point Processes and Gap Statistics for Translation Surfaces
paper.abstract: We study the behavior of saddle connection directions on translation surfaces from the point process viewpoint. We define a direction point process for saddle connections of length at most $R>0$ on every translation surface. Given a general ergodic $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb R)$-invariant measure $\mu$ on a stratum of translation surfaces, we also define a slope point process associated with $\mu$. By utilizing the dynamics and geometry of strata, we show that for almost every translation surface, the direction point processes, rescaled by $R^2$, converge in distribution to the slope point process as $R\to\infty$. Using Palm distribution theory, we prove the existence of limiting joint gap distributions and obtain new regularity results for gap distributions associated with the general $\mu$. Finally, we study how these point processes and joint gap distributions behave as the genus $g$ tends to infinity. In the principal stratum, we show that the slope point processes, rescaled by $g^2$, converge in distribution to a Poisson point process. By passing to the corresponding Palm distributions, we show that the rescaled slope gaps converge jointly to independent exponential random variables, which is in stark contrast to the known non-exponential gap distributions in a fixed genus.

paper.title: On the rank-one limit sets for maps in the constant-Jacobian shear group of $\mathbb{C}^2$
paper.abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}_c$ be the subgroup of $Aut(\mathbb{C}^2)$ generated by affine maps and shear automorphisms with constant Jacobian. We determine the possible conformal types of the rank-one limit set of an invariant recurrent Fatou component when the induced dynamics has infinite order. In particular we show that, under this infinite-order hypothesis, the limit set of a finite composition of H\'enon maps (polynomial or transcendental), can only be conformally equivalent to a disk or an annulus. Thus we exclude the remaining three conformal types, i.e. $\mathbb{D}^*$, $\mathbb{C}^*$ and $\mathbb{C}$, from the classification result by Arosio, Benini, Forn\ae ss and Peters. We also prove that the set of fixed points of a finite composition of H\'enon maps (polynomial or transcendental) contains no entire curves.

paper.title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
paper.abstract: Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics? The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.

paper.title: Simultaneously preperiodic points and colliding orbits for families of polynomials in characteristic $p$
paper.abstract: Let $k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and let $f\in k[X]$ be a polynomial of degree at least $2$ such that $f-f(0)$ is non-additive. For $\alpha,\beta$ in an algebraically closed extension $L$ of $k$, we prove that there are infinitely many $\lambda\in L$ for which both points are preperiodic under $f(X)+\lambda$ if and only if $\alpha,\beta\in k$ or $f(\beta)-f(\alpha)\in E_f$. Here $E_f=\{c\in G_f:(f-f(0))^n(c)\in G_f\text{ for every }n\ge0\}$, where $G_f=\{c\in k : f(X+c)-f(X)\in k\}$. We also provide a necessary and sufficient criterion for the corresponding colliding orbits set to be infinite.

paper.title: Theoretical and Computational Advances in Birkhoff Pseudospectral Transcription for Aerospace Optimal Control
paper.abstract: This paper develops theoretical and numerical extensions of Birkhoff pseudospectral transcription for aerospace optimal control problems. Building on the recently proposed body of knowledge, a Birkhoff integration operator is derived for flipped Legendre Gauss Radau (fLGR) grids, drawing connections to regular LGR grids and to the favorable conditioning properties that make Birkhoff interpolants particularly appealing. We also propose the enforcement of differential constraints via pseudospectral operators, and the primal and dual equivalence of this approach to state augmentation is established for control-rate limits. The numerical developments include the formulation and solution of heterogeneous multiphase optimal control problems, parameterized non-affine time mappings, composition of affine scaling and equilibration methods, and a hybrid derivative strategy to combine linear pseudospectral operators with numerical derivatives for nonlinear functions. These methods are implemented in the RAPTOR (Rapid Algorithm for Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimization and Robustification) transcription framework and assessed through feature-oriented benchmarks: a one-dimensional landing problem, a planar orbit-raising scenario, an atmospheric entry problem, and a multiphase reusable launch vehicle problem with simultaneous booster-recovery and upper-stage-insertion trajectories.

paper.title: Contractor Filters
paper.abstract: We introduce Contractor Filters (CFs), a set-membership architecture for nonlinear continuous-time state estimation with bounded uncertainties and sporadic outliers. CFs represent feasible states symbolically by compositions of contractors rather than rematerializing a geometric enclosure after each update. This provides an abstraction layer between the set-theoretic filtering equations and their numerical realization, so prediction, correction, ambiguity, and outlier handling can be expressed within one algebra without prescribing a state geometry. We derive an exact nominal recursion and a guaranteed robust enclosure, with validated flow inclusions preserving soundness. Optional sub-paving compression then provides finite outer representations. CFs are evaluated against a robust particle filter on range-only and terrain-based localization under outliers, probabilistic model mismatch, association ambiguity, and multimodality. CFs retain the simulated truth in all tested configurations, while particle-filter reliability degrades under persistent bias and spatial aliasing. Contractor strength and compression budget control the trade-off between paving tightness and computational cost, while preserving the enclosure guarantee.

paper.title: Degree growth of rational and meromorphic self-maps
paper.abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, or a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact K\"ahler manifold. We prove that in every codimension, the degree sequence of $f$ differs from its dynamical-degree growth by at most a polynomial factor, with an explicit universal bound on the polynomial exponent. In particular, subexponential but superpolynomial degree growth cannot occur. At a strict dynamical-degree break, we prove the sharper asymptotic \[ \mathrm{deg}_{i,\omega}(f^n)=C_{f,\omega,i}\,\lambda_i(f)^n+O(\eta^n), \] for every $\sqrt{\lambda_{i-1}(f)\lambda_{i+1}(f)}<\eta<\lambda_i(f)$. This extends the degree-asymptotic theorem of Dang--Favre from codimension one in characteristic zero to arbitrary codimension and arbitrary characteristic, and recovers the surface theorem of Boucksom--Favre--Jonsson. Both results rely on a uniform estimate for the temporal discrete logarithmic Laplacian of the degree sequences, obtained by applying the Ptolemy inequality to ordered Hodge--Lorentz packages on varying finite-time orbit spaces.
