paper.title: Square-Root Profiles and Sharp Fourier Decay of Quasiperiodic Spectral Measures
paper.abstract: We study spectral measures of one-dimensional quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators. For subcritical Schr\"odinger operator with Diophantine frequency, we prove sharp measurable-set bounds, answering a question of Avila and Jitomirskaya \cite{AJ}; we prove optimal Fourier decay and the sharp decay order of the time-averaged quantum return probability, confirming a conjecture of Aloisio, Carvalho, and de Oliveira \cite{ACO} and a prediction of Zhong and Mosseri \cite{ZhongMosseri}. For the subcritical almost Mathieu operator, we establish summable square-root envelopes for the spectral density, with an optimal density-one formulation of the lower bound, thereby answering a question of Avila \cite{Aqi}. These results follow from a general theorem for reflectionless measures under a summable square-root Craig-type condition. We establish an exact residue expansion of the squared Borel transform, which connects local density blow-up with long-time averaged return probabilities: the endpoint residues determine both the square-root edge profiles and the leading coefficient of the time-averaged return probability.

paper.title: The influence of decay in dynamic models of gene regulatory networks
paper.abstract: We investigate the influence of decay rates on the dynamics of three-dimensional gene regulatory networks modeled by nonlinear differential equations with logistic sigmoidal regulatory functions. Particular attention is paid to the existence, location, and stability of equilibrium points in systems involving numerous interacting parameters. An explicit analytical representation of a central equilibrium is obtained under suitable relations between the regulatory weights, thresholds, and decay coefficients, allowing its location to be determined without solving the corresponding nonlinear algebraic system numerically. General formulas for the characteristic polynomial of the linearized system are derived, and spectral conditions for instability are established for several classes of regulatory interactions. We demonstrate how variations in decay rates can change the number and stability of equilibria, transform oscillatory dynamics, and influence the emergence or suppression of complicated attractors. The possibility of chaotic behavior is investigated through eigenvalue configurations, Lyapunov exponents, and the Kaplan-Yorke dimension. Numerical examples illustrate the sensitivity of the dynamics to decay parameters, including the suppression of previously observed chaotic behavior. The results provide an analytical framework for investigating equilibrium configurations, stability transitions, and complex dynamics in parametrized gene regulatory networks.

paper.title: Stable manifolds of heteroclinic chains in Ho\v{r}ava-Lifshitz cosmology
paper.abstract: We consider vacuum spatially homogeneous models in Ho\v{r}ava-Lifshitz gravity, which are expected to describe generic singularities for these modified gravity theories. These models perturb the well-known Bianchi models in general relativity (GR) by a parameter $v\in (0,1)$, in which GR occurs at $v=1/2$. We show that all periodic heteroclinic chains of Bianchi type II orbits are robust for small perturbations of GR, i.e. they exist for any $v\approx 1/2$. Moreover, we prove the existence of a stable manifold for each heteroclinic chain within a Cantor set for the supercritical case, $v\in (1/2,1)$. In particular, we discuss the heteroclinic chains of periods three and four in detail.

paper.title: A parity constraint on the topological numbers of self-complementary triply-periodic surfaces
paper.abstract: The stability zone of Novikov's problem of planar sections of triply periodic surfaces are labeled by indivisible triples of integers, which we call the soul of the zone. Which triples may occur is not known. We show that, if a Morse function $f$ on $\mathbb T^3$ admits a translation $\tau(x)=x+v$ with $f\circ\tau=-f$, so that the sets $\{f<0\}$ and $\{f>0\}$ are congruent, then in the generic genus-$3$ situation every topological number $L$ satisfies $\langle L,2v\rangle\equiv1\pmod2$. The mechanism is that the electron/hole type of a null-homologous closed trajectory is invariant under the period lattice and is reversed by $\tau$. For $f=\cos2\pi x+\cos2\pi y+\cos2\pi z$ and the $\mu$-cube, this means that the sum of the components of each soul is odd.

paper.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
paper.abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. Moreover, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite $G$, and in particular for finite $G$, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.

analysis.relevance_note: Cellular automata over group shifts are central symbolic and group-action dynamics.
analysis.tldr: For locally finite groups, the authors characterize exactly when lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata.
analysis.problem: Determine the generated submonoid for alphabets with at least two symbols.
analysis.main_result: Equality fails for infinite alphabets or groups containing an infinite-order element, and for binary alphabets when the group has a Klein-four quotient. For locally finite groups, equality holds exactly for finite alphabets of size at least three, or for a binary alphabet when that quotient does not exist. Every surjective element of the generated monoid is invertible because lazy automata are never surjective.
analysis.context: Algebraic structure of cellular automata on group shifts.

paper.title: Global surfaces of section for dynamically convex Reeb flows on lens spaces
paper.abstract: We show that a dynamically convex Reeb flow on the standard tight lens space $(L(p, 1),\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$, $p>1,$ admits a $p$-unknotted closed Reeb orbit $P$ which is the binding of a rational open book decomposition with disk-like pages. Each page is a rational global surface of section for the Reeb flow and the Conley-Zehnder index of the $p$-th iterate of $P$ is $3$. We also check dynamical convexity in the H\'enon-Heiles system for low positive energies. In this case the rational open book decomposition follows from the fact that the sphere-like component of the energy surface admits a $\mathbb{Z}_{3}$-symmetric periodic orbit and the flow descends to a Reeb flow on the standard tight $(L(3,2),\xi_{\mathrm{std}})$.

analysis.relevance_note: Global surfaces of section and Reeb-flow topology connect to geometric dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Dynamically convex Reeb flows on standard tight lens spaces admit rational open books with disk-like global sections.

analysis.main_result: For \(p>1\) on the stated standard tight \(L(p,1)\), a \(p\)-unknotted orbit binds a disk-page rational open book; each page is a rational global section and the orbit's \(p\)-th iterate has Conley-Zehnder index three. A low-positive-energy Hénon-Heiles application uses a threefold-symmetric orbit and a descended lens-space Reeb flow. The energy threshold: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Contact-geometric flow topology and Hamiltonian global sections.

paper.title: Monochromatic non-commuting products
paper.abstract: We show that a finite coloring of an amenable group contains `many' monochromatic sets of the form $\{x,y,xy,yx\},$ and natural extensions with more variables. This gives the first combinatorial proof and extensions of Bergelson and McCutcheon's non-commutative Schur theorem. Our main new tool is the introduction of what we call `quasirandom colorings,' a condition that is automatically satisfied by colorings of quasirandom groups, and a reduction to this case.

analysis.tldr: Finite colorings of amenable groups contain many monochromatic noncommuting-product configurations and multivariable extensions.

analysis.main_result: The author gives a combinatorial proof and extensions of the noncommutative Schur theorem using quasirandom colorings and reduction to that case. The meaning and quantitative strength of many, and the precise multivariable patterns: Not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: An Approximate-Master-Equation Formulation of the Watts Threshold Model on Hypergraphs
paper.abstract: In traditional models of behavioral and opinion dynamics on networks, researchers suppose that interactions occur between pairs of individuals. However, in reality, social interactions also occur in sets of three or more individuals. A common way to incorporate such polyadic interactions is to study dynamical processes on hypergraphs, in which interactions can occur between any number of the individuals. A major current effort is to generalize popular dynamical processes from graphs to hypergraphs. One important model is the Watts threshold model (WTM), which describes a simplistic social spreading process and was extended recently by Chen et al. from dyadic networks (i.e., ordinary graphs) to polyadic networks (i.e., hypergraphs). In the present paper, we extend their discrete-time model to continuous time by using approximate master equations (AMEs). By employing AMEs, we are able to very accurately model the mean behavior of the continuous-time system. We reduce the high-dimensional AME system to a system of three coupled ordinary differential equations without any detectable loss of accuracy. This much lower-dimensional system is computationally faster to solve numerically, and it is also easier to interpret. We linearize the reduced AME system and derive a cascade condition, which allows us to determine when a large spreading event occurs. We then examine our reduced AME system on a contact hypergraph of a French primary school and on a hypergraph of computer-science coauthorships. We find that our full and reduced AME systems give reasonably good descriptions of the mean time-dependent fraction of active nodes in the polyadic WTM dynamics on these empirical networks.

paper.title: On the Kotani-Last Conjecture for the Dirac Operator
paper.abstract: We prove a dichotomy of almost periodicity for reflectionless one-dimensional Dirac operators whose spectra satisfy certain geometric conditions, extending work of Volberg--Yuditskii. We also construct a weakly mixing Dirac operator with a non-constant continuous potential whose spectrum is purely absolutely continuous, adapting Avila's argument for continuous Schr\"odinger operators. In particular, we disprove the Kotani--Last conjecture in the setting of one-dimensional Dirac operators.

analysis.tldr: The authors prove a reflectionless Dirac-operator almost-periodicity dichotomy and construct a weakly mixing example with purely absolutely continuous spectrum.
analysis.problem: Test almost periodicity and the Kotani-Last conjecture for one-dimensional Dirac operators.
analysis.main_result: Under certain unstated spectral geometric conditions, reflectionless operators satisfy an almost-periodicity dichotomy. A weakly mixing Dirac operator with nonconstant continuous potential and purely absolutely continuous spectrum disproves the conjecture in this setting.
methods: Adaptation of Avila's continuous Schrödinger-operator argument
analysis.context: One-dimensional Dirac spectral theory and weak mixing.

paper.title: Properness and finiteness of totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core
paper.abstract: We study totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core of geometrically finite rank-one locally symmetric manifolds. Although the infinite-volume setting can exhibit highly complicated behavior, including geodesic planes with fractal closures, we show that a strong rigidity persists inside the convex core. This rigidity has striking consequences in the infinite volume setting: every maximal totally geodesic submanifold of dimension at least two contained in the convex core is properly immersed and has finite volume, and only finitely many such submanifolds can occur. These results stand in sharp contrast to the behavior in the finite-volume setting. Moreover, combining this finiteness result with the work of Bader-Fisher-Miller-Stover and of Gromov-Schoen, we deduce that any geometrically finite rank-one manifold with infinitely many maximal totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two and of finite volume must be arithmetic.

analysis.relevance_note: Rigidity in rank-one locally symmetric spaces connects to homogeneous dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Maximal totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two contained in a geometrically finite convex core are properly immersed, finite-volume, and finite in number.
analysis.problem: Control totally geodesic submanifolds in infinite-volume convex cores.
analysis.main_result: For geometrically finite rank-one locally symmetric manifolds, the stated containment and dimension hypotheses imply proper immersion, finite volume, and finiteness. Combined with the cited rigidity work, infinitely many maximal finite-volume totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two force arithmeticity; these need not all lie inside the convex core.
methods: Combination with Bader-Fisher-Miller-Stover and Gromov-Schoen results
analysis.context: Geometric rigidity in rank-one locally symmetric manifolds, contrasted with fractal closure phenomena.

paper.title: Frobenius Revivals in Laplacian Cellular Automata: Replication, Entropy, and Information Recovery
paper.abstract: We investigate Frobenius revivals in prime-modulus Laplacian cellular automata. The Frobenius identity yields exact superpositions of translated, coefficient-weighted seed copies at prime-power times; we distinguish this algebraic replication from their geometric separation. We investigate seed recovery from separated replicas and evaluate the correction of independent symbol errors introduced during transmission of encoded configurations. For the diagonal neighborhood, we determine the exact periods of moving corner operators on square windows and establish sufficient conditions for recovering any binary seed under a binary--ternary--binary schedule. The results connect prime-power algebraic structure with spatial pattern formation and precisely delimited forms of information recovery.

analysis.tldr: Prime-power times yield exact weighted seed replication, while geometric separation governs the stated recovery results.
analysis.problem: Understand algebraic revivals and information recovery in prime-modulus Laplacian cellular automata.
analysis.main_result: The Frobenius identity yields superpositions of translated coefficient-weighted seed copies, distinct from geometric separation. For the diagonal neighborhood, moving-corner periods on square windows are determined and sufficient binary-ternary-binary recovery conditions are established for arbitrary binary seeds. Independent transmission errors are evaluated; exact periods and recovery conditions: Not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: On IDA-PBC with Maximum Energy Shapeability
paper.abstract: Interconnection and Damping Assignment Passivity-Based Control (IDA-PBC) is a well-established stabilization technique for affine nonlinear systems. However, its application is generally hindered by the requirement of solving a set of partial differential equations (PDEs), i.e., the so-called matching equation. This paper explores the notion of maximum energy shapeability which describes the scenario that the homogeneous part of the matching equation admits $m$ independent solutions with $m$ the dimension of the control input. We show that the maximum energy shapeability enables a systematic procedure for the IDA-PBC design by transforming the matching equation into a set of new PDEs. Specifically, the transformed matching equation admits an explicit solution in the single input case. Sufficient conditions for maximum energy shapeability are also provided. It is shown that some existing constructive IDA-PBC designs actually implicitly exploit the maximum energy shapeability. The proposed procedure for the IDA-PBC design is demonstrated with two practical examples.

analysis.relevance_note: Passivity-based energy-shaping control is not centrally connected to the strongest research interests.

paper.title: On Constructions of full-dimensional absolutely normal sets of uniqueness
paper.abstract: We construct a class of homogeneous Cantor-Moran measures with all contraction ratios being reciprocals of integers, and prove that they are pointwise absolutely normal. Our approach relies on methods developed by Davenport, Erd{\H{o}}s and LeVeque and properties of the order of integers in the multiplicative groups. The construction of these measures differs from the class of pointwise absolutely normal self-similar measures introduced by Hochman and Shmerkin, in which dynamical approaches were used. As an application, for all gauge functions $\varphi(r)$ with $r/\varphi(r)\to 0$ as $r\to 0$, we obtain a set of uniqueness $K$ with ${\mathcal H}^{\varphi}(K)>0$. Moreover, we show that there exists a pointwise absolutely normal measure $ \mu $ of dimension one fully supported on $ K $. The result shows that the simultaneous $\mathsf{DEL}$ control in every integer base can occur on a support that carries no nonzero Rajchman measure. Thus, the usual Fourier-decay mechanism for proving normality is sufficient but is far from necessary.

analysis.relevance_note: Full-dimensional Cantor-Moran measures, normality, and gauge Hausdorff measures are central.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct pointwise absolutely normal Cantor-Moran measures with reciprocal-integer contraction ratios and full-dimensional uniqueness-set applications.
analysis.problem: Combine absolute normality with supports that need not carry Rajchman measures.
analysis.main_result: For every gauge \(\varphi\) satisfying \(r/\varphi(r)\to0\) as \(r\to0\), the construction yields a uniqueness set \(K\) with \(\mathcal H^\varphi(K)>0\). A dimension-one pointwise absolutely normal measure is fully supported on \(K\), even though the support carries no nonzero Rajchman measure.
methods: Orders of integers in multiplicative groups
analysis.context: Fractal measures, absolute normality, and sets of uniqueness; Fourier decay is sufficient but unnecessary for the normality construction.

paper.title: Lyapunov characterization of boundedness of reachability sets for infinite-dimensional systems
paper.abstract: We prove a converse Lyapunov theorem for boundedness of reachability sets for a general class of control systems whose flow is Lipschitz continuous on compact intervals with respect to trajectory-dominated inputs. We show that this condition is satisfied by broad classes of semilinear evolution equations. For ordinary differential equations, as a consequence of our results, we obtain a converse Lyapunov theorem for forward completeness, without a priori restrictions on the magnitude of inputs. As an example, we rederive Wintner's classical result using our Lyapunov approach.

analysis.relevance_note: Reachability boundedness and converse Lyapunov results are control-centered without a stated central profile connection.

paper.title: Amplitude-Dependent Bode Diagrams via Scaled Relative Graphs
paper.abstract: Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) provide an intuitive graphical frequency-domain method for the analysis of Nonlinear (NL) systems, generalizing the Nyquist diagram. In this paper, we develop a method for computing $L_2$-gain bounds for Lur'e systems over bounded frequency and amplitude ranges. We do this by restricting the input space of the SRG both in frequency and energy content, and using methods from Sobolev theory. The resulting gain bounds over restricted sets of inputs are less conservative than bounds computed over the entire $L_2$, and yield three-dimensional NL generalization of the Bode diagram, plotting $L_2$-gain as function of both input frequency and energy content. In the zero-energy limit, the Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) Bode diagram is recovered, and at the infinite-energy zero-frequency limit, we recover the $L_2$-gain. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated on an example that resembles Phase-Locked Loop dynamics.

analysis.relevance_note: Amplitude-dependent nonlinear gain bounds are control and frequency-response analysis without a central profile connection.

paper.title: Counting the number of $1_{m}$-preperiodic $\mathcal{O}_{K}$-points of a discrete dynamical system with applications from arithmetic statistics, VII
paper.abstract: In this follow-up article of a multi-part series on (strictly) preperiodic point-counting, we inspect an astonishing relationship between the set of (strictly) $1_{m}$-preperiodic points of a polynomial map $\varphi_{d, c}$ defined by $\varphi_{d, c}(z) = z^d + c$ for all $c, z \in \mathcal{O}_{K}$ and the coefficient $c$, where $K$ is any number field of degree $n\geq 1$, $d>2$ is an integer and $m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is any fixed (eventual period). As before, we study counting problems that are inspired by torsion point-counting in arithmetic statistics and (strictly) preperiodic point-counting in arithmetic dynamics. In doing so, we then first prove that for any prime $p\geq 3$ and for any fixed $\ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ and fixed (eventual period) $m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, the average number of distinct $1_{m}$-preperiodic integral points of any $\varphi_{p^{\ell}, c}$ modulo prime $p\mathcal{O}_{K}$ is unbounded or zero as $c\to \infty$. Inspired further by work of Doyle-Poonen along with conjectural work of Hutz and $\textit{abc}(\textit{d})$-conditional work of Panraksa on $K$-rational preperiodic points of any $\varphi_{(p-1)^{\ell}, c}$ for any prime $p\geq 5$ in arithmetic dynamics, we then also prove that for any fixed (eventual period) $m \in \mathbb{Z}_{ \geq 1}$, the average number of distinct $1_{m}$-preperiodic integral points of any $\varphi_{(p-1)^{\ell}, c}$ modulo prime $p\mathcal{O}_{K}$ is unbounded or zero as $c\to \infty$. Finally, we then apply counting and distribution results from arithmetic statistics, and then get counting and statistical results on arithmetic objects arising naturally in our polynomial discrete dynamical settings. Together with the previous articles in the series, it might then be fair to view this article as an attempt to contribute to "arithmetic statistical dynamics".

paper.title: Cantor Spectrum via a Reducibility-Duality Bridge for the Mosaic Almost Mathieu Operator
paper.abstract: We study the mosaic Almost Mathieu operator, a quasiperiodic model that naturally admits a singular strip-Jacobi representation. By establishing a duality framework and extending the correspondence between the integrated density of states and the fibered rotation number to this setting, we obtain an effective reduction to $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ cocycles. As a consequence, combining Aubry duality, reducibility theory, and the Moser--P\"oschel argument, we prove that the spectrum is a Cantor set for all noncritical parameters.

analysis.tldr: The mosaic almost Mathieu spectrum is a Cantor set for every noncritical parameter, via a reducibility-duality bridge.
analysis.problem: Extend duality and rotation-number methods to a singular strip-Jacobi representation.
analysis.main_result: A duality framework and correspondence between integrated density of states and fibered rotation number reduce the problem to real special-linear two-dimensional cocycles. Aubry duality, reducibility, and the Moser-Pöschel argument then give Cantor spectrum at all noncritical parameters. The critical-parameter definition and other parameter hypotheses: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Quasiperiodic operators and cocycle dynamics.

paper.title: Stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of PDEs with Burgers-type nonlinearity
paper.abstract: We investigate the stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of nonlinear evolution equations sharing a Burgers-type convective nonlinearity and a polynomial linear differential operator, including the Burgers, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Kawahara, Benney--Lin, and Nikolaevskiy equations. Under periodic boundary conditions, each equation is represented through a Fourier truncation of order $K$, yielding a real state of one-sided complex Fourier coefficients, which is coupled to a slave system driven by observed master data. We first establish local exponential stability of the deterministic zero-error synchronization solution under a simple condition on the coupling strength in the slave model. We then introduce observational noise in the coupling signals, which turns the slave system into an It\^o diffusion and prevents exact synchronization. Comparing the stochastic synchronization error with the deterministic reference error obtained from noiseless observations, we show that bounded master and reference paths and sufficiently strong scalar coupling yield an $\mathcal O(\sigma^2)$ mean-square bound on their deviation, together with a tail-probability estimate; the bound becomes time-uniform when the deterministic slave field and its spatial derivative can be bounded uniformly in time. Both results use a Fourier-space norm induced by the physical-space $L^2$-norm, so Parseval's identity transfers the spectral bounds directly to the physical fields. Under additional regularity assumptions on the smoothness of the deterministic master and slave fields, we also obtain a mean-square bound on the stochastic synchronization error with respect to the infinite-dimensional (non-truncated) master system. These analytical results are illustrated by the numerical simulation of two master--slave systems, built around the Kawahara and Nikolaevskiy equations.

analysis.relevance_note: Noise robustness of PDE synchronization is applied stability analysis without a central profile connection.

paper.title: Parameter estimation in differential equations: Mathematical foundations for satellite gravimetry, review and perspectives
paper.abstract: Satellite gravimetry has become essential in many areas of earth science. However, the resolution of satellite gravitational models remains low at scales of a few hundreds km and no gravity recovery methods can take full advantages of unprecedented high accuracy of satellite tracking measurements. We first provide a unified theoretical framework of parameter estimation in differential equations for satellite gravimetry and then briefly review the mathematical methods to compute the gravity field of the Earth from satellite tracking. We focus on the collocation method, Kaula linear perturbations, two-point boundary value problems and orbit-energy-based methods. The numerical integration method is also included in this review, though it has been proved to be mathematically incorrect and physically not permitted. The reason is that it has become the standard method to routinely produce global gravitational models from satellite tracking data, which have been widely applied in many different areas of earth science. Because it is not clear how the incorrect foundation would affect gravity products from satellite tracking, we do not review any applications of these products. We then present a measurement-based perturbation theory to estimate the gravity field of the Earth, which can fully utilize both precise satellite orbits of arbitrary length and unprecedented high accuracy of satellite and inter-satellite tracking. The method is theoretically free of modeling errors, is capable of extracting any small forces from satellite and inter-satellite tracking data and provides a guarantee for high-precision and high-resolution global gravity models. Finally, we assume a reference gravity model and derive local solutions to the Newton's nonlinear governing differential equations of satellite motion for scattered tracking data that can still be important in some applications.

analysis.relevance_note: Satellite-gravimetry parameter estimation is applied differential-equation modeling without a central profile connection.

paper.title: Mean-Field Oscillator Ising Machines: Gradient Flows and Classification of Limit Solutions
paper.abstract: Oscillator Ising Machines (OIMs) have emerged as promising computational architectures for approximating solutions to combinatorial optimization problems. We derive and analyze the mean-field limit of an OIM model and show that it inherits the gradient flow structure of the finite-dimensional dynamics. We identify conditions under which this mean-field evolution admits an Eulerian formulation as a gradient flow on the Wasserstein space of probability measures and contrast this with a Lagrangian formulation which is always available. This gradient flow structure strongly constrains the long-time dynamics and enables a complete classification of limit solutions and their stability in the totally symmetric case. In particular, all limit solutions are fixed points whose phases cluster into at most four groups, and for almost all parameter values, only binarized fixed points -- those with clusters at $0$ and/or $\pi$ -- can be stable. Since binarized states are exactly those for which a feasible solution to the original problem can be read out, this shows that feasible solutions can almost always be recovered. We provide tight bounds on the parameter thresholds for which fixed points in this binarized family are stable, thereby identifying the threshold for binarization in this model, and present numerical evidence that the mean-field model correctly predicts behavioral regimes in certain large random networks, including Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi networks. Moreover, this problem provides a case study in the application of mean-field models, gradient flows, and optimal transport to the study of large-scale systems, and we highlight a number of features of this problem which are informative in this respect.

analysis.relevance_note: Gradient dynamics on probability-measure spaces and limit-state classification provide a possible invariant-measure connection.
analysis.tldr: The mean-field oscillator Ising model inherits gradient structure and, in the totally symmetric case, admits a complete limit-state and stability classification.
analysis.problem: Describe the mean-field long-time behavior and binarization threshold of oscillator Ising machines.
analysis.main_result: A Lagrangian gradient formulation is always available, while an Eulerian Wasserstein formulation requires unstated conditions. In the totally symmetric case, limit solutions are fixed points with at most four phase clusters; for almost all parameter values only clusters at zero and/or pi can be stable. Tight stability thresholds are given without their formulas; predictions for some large random networks are numerical evidence.
analysis.context: Optimization-oriented oscillator dynamics and evolution of probability measures.

paper.title: Sparse Koopman Autoencoders Identify Local Dynamical Regimes in Multibasin Systems
paper.abstract: Koopman autoencoders (KAEs) seek a higher-dimensional latent representation in which nonlinear dynamics evolve linearly. However, many interesting systems have multiple basins of attraction, and both theoretical and empirical work has shown these multibasin systems cannot generally admit a single finite-dimensional global Koopman embedding under standard assumptions. We posit that encoders with a sparsity-inducing objective encouraging few active latent coefficients will provide latent supports as an inspectable basin-modeling principle for Koopman autoencoders. We use these encoders producing sparse latents in training Sparse Koopman Autoencoders (SKAEs) without basin labels or other regime annotations, and treat the learned latent supports as model-produced regime variables after training. Across a range of procedurally generated multibasin systems and chaotic flows, we show that SKAEs have superior forecasting performance compared to dense-latent KAEs. We also perform a mechanistic study that shows latent supports produced by SKAEs are both essential for the quality of the representation and useful for identifying basins on basin-interior states, whereas dense-latent KAEs collapse to an uninformative single support family. These results identify sparse latents and their corresponding supports as label-free, interpretable regime variables for Koopman learning in nonlinear systems with multiple local dynamical laws.

analysis.relevance_note: Sparse Koopman autoencoders focus on empirical forecasting and basin identification rather than a central entropy, symbolic, or dimension-theory result.
